profiles.title: Astro content site
profiles.summary: Content-first websites that pre-render public pages and hydrate selected interactive islands.
profiles.shape: Astro · TypeScript · Content Collections when structured
use_cases: Documentation, guides, blogs, catalogs and marketing sites with repeatable authored content
Content-first websites that need a few independent interactive widgets
Public pages that can be generated at build time and served as static files
choose_when: Most routes present content and should be available as generated HTML without a request-time application server
Markdown or structured local data needs schema validation and generated routes
Interactivity is limited to discrete components that can hydrate independently
The team wants TypeScript templates while retaining ordinary HTML, CSS and browser APIs
avoid_when: The site is a tiny stable page set with no recurring content or build workflow; plain HTML and CSS may be enough
The main product is a sustained stateful browser application such as an inbox, dashboard or collaborative editor; choose a browser-app framework around that requirement

Request-time identity, private personalized pages, mutations, APIs, database writes, durable jobs or transactional effects are required and no separately owned backend or selected Astro adapter is in scope
Nontechnical editors need a managed editorial interface, preview, approval and media workflow; choose and qualify the CMS as content owner before selecting a presentation layer
profiles.tradeoff: Static output needs a separate owner for request-time identity, private data, writes and durable work.
profiles.evidence_status: documentation-reviewed; disposable create-astro basics scaffold, install, build and local dev HTTP smoke check executed; no application integration tests run

profiles.title: Phoenix + LiveView
profiles.summary: Connected products, live updates and background work in one application.
choose_when: Server-owned state and business rules dominate a connected product.
Phoenix conventions and OTP process lifecycles match the service requirements.
A relational store can also support durable background jobs.
avoid_when: The main deliverable is a platform-native mobile UI or offline-first client.
The application depends on a library, accelerator or vendor SDK unsupported by the intended Elixir deployment.
A small static site, simple script or CLI does not need a running web application.
profiles.tradeoff: A persistent server owns the UI state. Use a separate client for substantial offline work.

profiles.title: Next.js
profiles.summary: React interfaces with server rendering, routes and application logic.
use_cases: Browser applications with owned APIs and relational data
choose_when: Shared TypeScript contracts and React UI are useful
Server rendering or a web-facing backend is required
Team accepts explicit server/client and cache boundaries
avoid_when: Only static editorial content is required
Existing API already owns all backend responsibilities and SSR is unnecessary
Native mobile or desktop UI is the deliverable
profiles.tradeoff: Server/client boundaries, caching and deployment adapters need deliberate design.

profiles.title: React + Vite
profiles.summary: An interactive browser app connected to an existing or separate API.
choose_when: Backend/identity already have owners
SSR is not a product requirement
Browser UI and API can be deployed independently
avoid_when: Searchable server-rendered content is central
The task requires native device UI
Team expects the frontend scaffold to supply backend auth or persistence
profiles.tradeoff: This is a frontend. Your backend still owns identity, data permissions and durable work.

profiles.title: Rails + Hotwire
profiles.summary: Database-backed products with HTML, accounts and jobs close together.
choose_when: An integrated monolith and server-owned UI fit the product.
A small team benefits from stable conventions and limited integration work.
avoid_when: The core is an offline-first canvas or requires extensive browser-owned state.
Hard CPU/latency constraints justify a specialist service.
profiles.tradeoff: Rich offline or canvas-heavy interfaces can need a separate client.

profiles.title: Laravel + Livewire
profiles.summary: PHP product applications with a cohesive UI, auth and queue toolset.
choose_when: PHP team or Laravel ecosystem fit is strong.
Integrated auth, queues and concrete agent inspection tools reduce assembly work.
avoid_when: The UI fundamentally requires an offline/client-state architecture; use the Inertia alternative if Laravel still fits.
A hosting plan cannot operate needed queue workers or scheduled jobs.
profiles.tradeoff: The web process, queue workers and scheduler each need deployment supervision.

profiles.title: Django
profiles.summary: Data-heavy products with an ORM, forms, accounts and admin.
choose_when: Accounts, forms, admin and database workflows are central
A cohesive conventional monolith reduces integration decisions
avoid_when: Only a small stateless endpoint is needed
The core workload needs a different runtime or hard real-time guarantees
profiles.tradeoff: Interactive clients and long-running jobs require their own interface and worker choices.

profiles.title: Go service
profiles.summary: HTTP APIs and backend services with a straightforward binary deployment.
choose_when: Prefer explicit service code and standard tooling
Kubernetes or Go infrastructure integration matters
PostgreSQL already owns business state
avoid_when: Need a batteries-included product framework
Hard real-time or no-GC constraints
Rich client UI is the primary product
profiles.tradeoff: Product features such as authorization and administration need explicit assembly.

profiles.title: Rust service
profiles.summary: Services where runtime control and explicit resource handling matter.
choose_when: Memory/resource control or Rust library reuse is important
Team accepts ownership/async complexity for compile-time guarantees
avoid_when: Primary goal is conventional CRUD delivery with minimal framework assembly
Team cannot maintain Rust async code
A full product framework is needed immediately
profiles.tradeoff: Async runtime and type complexity add development work; measure the reason to choose them.

profiles.title: FastAPI
profiles.summary: Typed Python APIs alongside Python integrations, data or AI libraries.
use_cases: HTTP endpoints for model or worker products
choose_when: API contracts and Python integrations matter more than built-in product/admin UI
A separate frontend or service boundary already exists
avoid_when: The team mostly needs accounts, admin, forms and CRUD that Django supplies
Blocking or CPU-intensive jobs would be run inside request event loops
profiles.tradeoff: Authentication, migrations and durable jobs are separate integration decisions.

profiles.title: Go CLI + TUI
profiles.summary: Command-line applications and terminal interfaces distributed as binaries.
profiles.shape: Cobra · Bubble Tea when needed · GoReleaser
choose_when: Want compiled distribution with Go ecosystem access
Command structure and terminal UX matter more than tight low-level control
avoid_when: Primarily a short disposable script
Host SDK or native UI framework mandates another language
Strict no-GC constraints
profiles.tradeoff: Test every target platform; interactive terminals and redirected output have different needs.

profiles.title: Rust CLI + TUI
profiles.summary: Portable command-line tools with explicit memory and resource control.
choose_when: Need native performance or reuse of Rust libraries
Want ownership/type checks around complex transformations
avoid_when: Disposable automation would be simpler in Python or shell
Build latency and cross-toolchains outweigh runtime needs
profiles.tradeoff: Cross-compilation and native dependencies still need target-specific qualification.

profiles.title: Python automation + AI
profiles.summary: Scripts, integrations and workers close to the Python data and AI ecosystem.
profiles.shape: uv · Pydantic · HTTPX / provider SDK · pytest
choose_when: The deliverable is a bounded task or worker rather than a web product
Python SDKs or data libraries materially simplify integrations
avoid_when: A one-off script is being expanded into an undocumented product backend
Hard real-time deadlines or a native deployment requirement dominate
profiles.tradeoff: Persistent workers need an execution platform; model outputs and tool calls need validation.

profiles.title: Swift + SwiftUI
profiles.summary: Native iPhone and iPad apps using Apple's UI and platform APIs.
use_cases: Accessible mobile clients for a shared service
choose_when: Apple-native UI and platform capabilities are requirements
A Mac/Xcode build environment and Apple distribution ownership are available
avoid_when: The requirement is a single shared UI across iOS and Android
There is no supported macOS/Xcode build environment
profiles.tradeoff: Apple builds and distribution need macOS/Xcode; Android needs its own client.

profiles.title: Kotlin + Compose
profiles.summary: Native Android apps with platform UI, lifecycle and storage integration.
use_cases: Accessible mobile clients for a shared service
choose_when: Android-native UI and platform behavior are requirements
The team can own an Android SDK, emulator/device and signed release pipeline
avoid_when: The requirement is a single shared UI for Android and iOS
No Android device or emulator verification can be performed
profiles.tradeoff: Device diversity and background restrictions need Android-specific checks; iOS is a separate client.
